s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with erosions and scarring, localized to one area of the body
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Lesions localized to the left shin
Lesions have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are itchy
Milia are present in the superficial dermis
Erosions with partially detached epidermis are present
Dermoepidermal separation is present on histopathologic examination
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene

shortlist.label: Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, progressive, itchy skin lesions with erosions and scarring, localized to one area of the body, match the clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Dominant Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene and presence of milia and dermoepidermal separation support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of erosions, scarring, and dermoepidermal separation, along with the genetic variant in COL7A1, make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Itchy skin lesions with erosions could be consistent with bullous pemphigoid, although the localized nature and genetic findings make it less likely

shortlist.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic, itchy skin lesions with erosions could be seen in linear IgA bullous dermatosis, but the lack of mucous membrane involvement and specific genetic findings make it less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of itchy, erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques localized to the left shin, along with milia and erosions, and the novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene, are consistent with Epidermolysis Bullosa Pruriginosa (EBP), a subtype of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa characterized by pruriginous lesions.

rejected.label: Dominant Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: While the COL7A1 gene mutation is consistent with dominant dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, the specific clinical presentation and localization of lesions are more characteristic of EBP.

rejected.label: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes EBP, but the specific features of the case, such as the pruritic nature of the lesions and their localization, point more specifically to EBP.

rejected.label: Bullous Pemphigoid
rejected.why: The clinical and histopathological findings, including the presence of milia and the specific genetic mutation, do not align with bullous pemphigoid, which typically involves autoantibodies against components of the basement membrane zone.

rejected.label: Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by linear IgA deposits along the basement membrane zone, which is not mentioned in the case, and the clinical presentation and genetic findings do not align with this diagnosis.
